questions.q: A monopsony is a market with:
questions.ok: Correct: A single or dominant buyer.
questions.fb: A single or dominant buyer. Review the Learn tab.

questions.q: A monopsony employer hires workers up to the point where:
questions.ok: Correct: It equates marginal cost of labour with marginal revenue product.
questions.fb: It equates marginal cost of labour with marginal revenue product. Review the Learn tab.

questions.q: Compared with a competitive labour market, a monopsony employer pays:
opts: A higher wage and employs more
A lower wage and employs fewer
A lower wage and employs more
questions.ok: Correct: It restricts employment and pays the supply-curve wage.
questions.fb: It restricts employment and pays the supply-curve wage. Review the Learn tab.
questions.model: A lower wage and employs fewer

questions.q: A minimum wage between the monopsony wage and the competitive wage is likely to:
questions.ok: Correct: MCL becomes flat at the minimum wage until the supply curve.
questions.fb: MCL becomes flat at the minimum wage until the supply curve. Review the Learn tab.

opts: Low barriers to entry and exit

questions.fb: Low barriers allow hit-and-run entry. Review the Learn tab.

questions.q: In a contestable market incumbents are likely to:
opts: Keep price close to average cost
questions.fb: To deter entry. Review the Learn tab.

questions.q: Which is a strategic barrier to entry?
